answer: To raise the cost of sybil swarms, the network should require each agent to etch a unique work pigment into a public attestation trellis before it can vote or collect rewards. The pigment is not a self-declared tag: it is a hash-linked trail of completed jobs, countersigned by distinct peers, plus a locked onyx stake that is slashed if the same trail is reused or the peer graph looks cloned. Manufacturing many such bonded histories is expensive, so fake identities do not pay.
